children.text: tmux kind of is that daemon. The agent keeps running on the box and I attach from my laptop or phone. What I was missing was everything around it, like paste and files.

Isn't this the wrong architecture? Fundamentally, a coding agent should be running as a headless/detached process, a daemon. If it needs a CLI then that CLI can attach/connect to that daemon and interact with it. If you architect it that way then you can quit and resume the CLI anytime you want, from any machine you want and with whatever UI you want, the daemon doesn't care. Running the agent as an interactive CLI process which you need to stuff into something like tmux is just the wrong approach, and "connecting" to it by reading/scraping its screen is terrible.

I put tailscale on my desktop and run my AI sessions in tmux (or per that other HN topic, anything with persistent attachable sessions).
Now I can termux in from my phone or laptop and keep the work going. Not everyone has a spare desktop sitting around, but I like having freedom of provider and keeping the actual filesystem on my machine.

You can just install Claude Code on the server and drive it from Claude Desktop via remote control. That way you can control Claude Code on mutiple servers straight from your Claude Desktop, Mobile or Web, and stay fully within Anthropic tools.

Everything works: you get the native view of subagents, you can upload files and images, fork threads, etc.

The massive upside is that the actual work happens on the server so you can close your laptop and it will continue plus it will not fry your thighs. The advantage over sessions (which I haven't tried but theoretically sound) is that you can configure Claude's environment on the server however you like. Give it any tools you need, ssh access to other machines, sudo, whatever.

The only downside is that every new project requires a setup step on the server (to add the systemd service) where you will develop it since Claude can only handle one server per directory. Claude will handle this step however if you give it ssh access to your server.

The machines show up nicely in Claude Desktop/Mobile/Web, and repos/projects are in a dropdown. Unless you work on very many projects at the same time, this setup is golden.

children.text: Interesting. I’ve been using it heavily on macOS (ssh to Linux host) and over the web using xterm.js, and it’s been working about as reliably as tmux did. Sometimes it doesn’t resize properly, but that’s also true of tmux (when I see a big field of .).
I want to like shpool but it struggles with reattaching and redrawing or resizing

I've been using shpool these days (especially for things like Claude / Codex / etc). Shpool only does persistence, not multiplexing. It turns out this is exactly what I want. I want to have one keyboard shortcut, to detach the session, and that's it.

I can do terminal multiplexing better in the GUI—tabs, virtual desktops, or in the browser with xterm.js.

Yes, you can learn all these different tmux shortcuts, and I know them well enough. I like using the shortcuts in my terminal emulator better. All I really want is a way to continue my session after putting my laptop to sleep, and shpool does exactly that and no more.

children.author: benfrancom
children.text: It's always been a chore to keep sessions (and tmux windows) at a minimum to avoid context switching and the cognitive drag/fatigue that comes with too many. My goal is 2 active sessions to avoid context switching, but it's so easy to just take on more tasks and try to cycle between all of them, and accomplish less overall. I've had upwards of a dozen, and it is very draining. Even more panes within windows to track subtasks becomes unruly. The other problem is that work keeps ballooning as agents pick up related/unplanned work along the way all the time. I try to reign things in by having the agent create tickets that we will revisit during planning sessions later. By keeping tasks minimal, it feels slower, but then I can think deeply about the problem without the cognitive residue coming from all the other sessions.
